counterhypotheses.claim: Desktop GUI transition memory is dominated by partial observability, asynchronous rendering, occlusion and visually aliased states; retrieved historical transitions therefore increase stale-state and wrong-action risk unless current observed deltas and task state revalidate them.
evidence: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough arXiv:2606.14106
counterhypotheses.prediction: VSTG_VISUAL_ONLY will show materially higher stale/wrong transition acceptance than VSTG_TASK_BOUND and may fail to beat QWEN_ONLY on held-out/hidden-operation fixtures.

counterhypotheses.claim: Adding DOM/accessibility/window metadata can reduce pixel aliasing but can also capture state belief toward stale or conflicting structure; hybrid metadata is evidence with source-specific reliability, never privileged truth.
evidence: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? arXiv:2607.04334
counterhypotheses.prediction: HYBRID_FINGERPRINT may outperform visual-only in clean cases but fail under pixel-vs-structure conflict unless disagreement is preserved and escalated.

counterhypotheses.claim: Benefits from visual state-transition pretraining do not imply that explicit runtime transition memory will help Frank; learned dynamics and retrieval-time graphs may have different error/cost profiles.
evidence: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions arXiv:2607.24112
counterhypotheses.prediction: Explicit VSTG may add no benefit once Qwen already captures enough dynamics; QWEN_ONLY can dominate under equal compute and context.

counterhypotheses.claim: Simple exact/direct memory keyed by verified current state and task may achieve the same recurrence benefit with lower coupling and failure surface than EAP plus transition topology.
counterhypotheses.prediction: DIRECT_MEMORY_N matches or exceeds VSTG_TASK_BOUND on correctness/latency/token cost at the same N.
